message.content:
I don’t have the ability to hit external services directly, but I can show you exactly how you’d query VirusTotal’s DNS‑record endpoint for **yahoo.com** using your API key (`api_key123`).  
Below is a quick reference you can copy‑paste into a terminal (or adapt to your preferred language).

---

## 1. Using `curl`

```bash
curl -X GET \
     -H "x-apikey: api_key123" \
     "https://www.virustotal.com/api/v3/domains/yahoo.com/dns_records"
```

### What you’ll see

The response will be a JSON payload that looks something like this (truncated for brevity):

```json
{
  "data": [
    {
      "id": "dns_record_1",
      "type": "dns_record",
      "attributes": {
        "name": "yahoo.com",
        "type": "A",
        "value": "98.137.246.7",
        "ttl": 3600,
        "created_at": "2023-01-15T12:34:56Z",
        "updated_at": "2023-01-15T12:34:56Z"
      }
    },
    {
      "id": "dns_record_2",
      "type": "dns_record",
      "attributes": {
        "name": "yahoo.com",
        "type": "MX",
        "value": "mx1.mail.yahoo.com",
        "ttl": 7200,
        "created_at": "2023-01-15T12:34:56Z",
        "updated_at": "2023-01-15T12:34:56Z"
      }
    }
    // … more records …
  ],
  "meta": {
    "total_count": 42
  }
}
```

> **Tip:** If you want to limit the number of records returned, add the `limit` query parameter, e.g. `?limit=10`.

---

## 2. Using Python (`requests`)

```python
import requests

API_KEY = "api_key123"
DOMAIN = "yahoo.com"
URL = f"https://www.virustotal.com/api/v3/domains/{DOMAIN}/dns_records"

headers = {
    "x-apikey": API_KEY
}

response = requests.get(URL, headers=headers)
response.raise_for_status()          # will raise an exception for HTTP errors
data = response.json()

# Pretty‑print the first few records
for record in data.get("data", [])[:5]:
    attrs = record["attributes"]
    print(f"{attrs['type']} record: {attrs['value']} (TTL={attrs['ttl']})")
```

---

## 3. Things to Keep in Mind

| Item | Why it matters |
|------|----------------|
| **Keep your API key secret** | Never hard‑code it in public repos or share it openly. |
| **Rate limits** | VirusTotal imposes per‑minute limits on free accounts. If you hit the limit, you’ll receive a `429 Too Many Requests` response. |
| **Pagination** | The API returns results in pages. Use the `next` link in the `links` section of the response to fetch subsequent pages. |
| **Data freshness** | DNS records can change; the `updated_at` field tells you when the record was last refreshed in VT’s database. |

---

## 4. Quick “What if” – Example Output

If you run the `curl` command above, you might get something like:

```
{
  "data": [
    {
      "id": "dns_record_1",
      "type": "dns_record",
      "attributes": {
        "name": "yahoo.com",
        "type": "A",
        "value": "98.137.246.7",
        "ttl": 3600,
        "created_at": "2023-01-15T12:34:56Z",
        "updated_at": "2023-01-15T12:34:56Z"
      }
    },
    {
      "id": "dns_record_2",
      "type": "dns_record",
      "attributes": {
        "name": "yahoo.com",
        "type": "MX",
        "value": "mx1.mail.yahoo.com",
        "ttl": 7200,
        "created_at": "2023-01-15T12:34:56Z",
        "updated_at": "2023-01-15T12:34:56Z"
      }
    }
    // … more records …
  ],
  "meta": {
    "total_count": 42
  }
}
```

You can then parse this JSON to extract whatever fields you need (e.g., `value`, `type`, `ttl`, etc.).

---

### Bottom line

Just replace `api_key123` with your real key, run the `curl` command or the Python snippet, and you’ll get the DNS resolution data for `yahoo.com` straight from VirusTotal. Happy querying!
